editorial:
Imagine a world where a wealthy newspaper owner pretends to be a criminal to fight crime from the inside. That is the setup here, featuring a secret identity and a cool car. You get to see a hero and his sidekick take on gangs in a style that feels like an old-school comic book. The vibe is a weird mix of a detective show and an action flick, but it feels very choppy because it was actually made from old TV episodes. It is less of a polished movie and more of a strange time capsule from the sixties and seventies.

If you love Bruce Lee, you will probably enjoy seeing his fighting skills, even if the editing is a mess. You will notice that the screen is cropped poorly, so people's heads are often cut off at the top. It is a bumpy ride with a confusing plot, but it has a certain charm for fans of odd cinema. If you want to check it out, try renting it on Apple TV or hunting down a physical copy for your collection. Just go into it knowing it is a bit of a disaster, and you will have a fun time laughing at how strange it is.
endingExplained: The story wraps up with the hero and his partner finally taking down the bad guys after a series of messy fights. Since the movie is just spliced-together TV episodes, the ending feels abrupt. You see the criminals get arrested and the city returns to normal. There is no big shocking twist, just a simple victory for the good guys that leaves the door open for more adventures that never really happen in this format.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves Bruce Lee or old TV shows.
